# `project_erp_links`

> **GENERATED** — rendered from the data contract. Edit [`supabase/contract/project_erp_links.contract.yaml`](../../../supabase/contract/project_erp_links.contract.yaml)

**Tier G** — governance — identity, capability, delegation, audit · owned by `data-ingestion` · `public.project_erp_links`

**One row is** One authorized link between one project and one company in one external system: project ownership proved on this side, company membership proved on that side by the linking user's own OAuth consent. One link is one credential and one project — never shared, so revoking one project's link cannot be bypassed by a sibling.

NOT RENAMED BY WP 3.1, AND THAT IS A DECISION. The four tables around it became `ingest_*` because they hold rows from ANY source; this one holds the credential and the consent for ONE source, and calling it `ingest_links` would promise a generality it does not have — a CSV upload has nothing to link. When a second connector arrives, the question to ask is whether it shares this shape (a per-user delegated token proving membership of an external tenant) or needs its own; `ingest_runs.source_kind` already carries the distinction that matters to everything downstream. ITS SIDECAR IS HERE BECAUSE WP 3.1 IS WHERE IT WAS DUE. The table was deferred under this package in `coverage.yaml` since WP 1.4, and a deferral is a commitment: carrying it forward to the next open package would have been the same move that produced D41 — an owner who has gone home, indistinguishable from an owner.

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | **no user-facing write path** |
| Minimum project role | `editor` |
| Tier transitions audited | **no** — invariant `audit-actor` is not met here yet |
| Row-level security | **cannot be determined from the migrations** |
| Policies on the table | 1 — all carry a predicate |

One FOR ALL policy — `has_project_access(project_id)` — so reading and writing a link are the same permission: whoever can administer the project can connect it to a source and disconnect it. That is deliberate and it is also the loosest thing on this page, because `min_project_role: owner` is the intent and nothing enforces a project role yet (WP 2.2 landed the resolver; no policy here calls it). `audited: false` is the one that should be uncomfortable: creating a link grants an external system standing access to a project's data and revoking one takes it away, and neither writes an audit row. It is not a tier transition, so G4 does not formally cover it; it is a governance event by any reading of §5, and it is recorded here as a named gap rather than left to be noticed. The table's own honesty is elsewhere and it is real: `status`, `status_detail`, `last_verified_at` and `revoked_at` mean a revoked link says when and why. NO `rls_enabled` FIELD, and its absence is the point. The connector migration enables RLS on this table in a plain statement and creates its policy in another — but the same file also builds the staging policies inside a `DO $$ EXECUTE format(...) $$` loop whose SQL mentions this table, so the introspector marks its RLS indeterminate: "the migrations do not say", which is a different claim from "off" and may not be rendered as one. Only the live database can answer (§15), and a sidecar may not assert what the schema does not settle.

> of the migration history cannot evaluate. The honest answer is *unknown*, and this
> page will not round it to *off*: a security review that starts from an invented
